title: BNCI 2025-002 Continuous 2D Trajectory Decoding dataset
description: This dataset comprises continuous 2D trajectory decoding from attempted arm movements recorded via 60-channel EEG from 10 participants (9 able-bodied, 1 with spinal cord injury) across 3 sessions. Participants performed motor imagery tasks including target-tracking (snakerun) and self-paced shape tracing (freerun) with visual feedback, providing a resource for investigating learning effects and neuroprosthetic control in motor decoding. The preprocessed data includes temporal and source-localized features suitable for regression-based trajectory prediction models.
methods_description: EEG was recorded at 200 Hz from 60 channels (actiCAP, Brain Products) with right mastoid reference and Fpz ground. Preprocessing included anti-aliasing (25 Hz) and notch (50 Hz) filtering, downsampling to 100 Hz, bad channel interpolation, eye artifact subtraction (SGEYESUB), removal of frontal channels, high-pass filtering (0.18 Hz), common average re-referencing, drift attenuation (HEAR algorithm), low-pass filtering (3 Hz), and final downsampling to 20 Hz. Feature extraction employed temporal features (7 time points × 55 channels) and sLORETA source localization. Decoding used PLS regression with UKF smoothing.
